prompt: Independently re-encode regulation 4 of the Accident Compensation (Earners' Levy) Regulations 2025 (NZ) in rulespec/v1 format, working only from the pinned axiom-corpus release nz-rulespec-2026-07-20 statute XML and without reading the rulespec-nz project's published encoding at any point during encoding; then, in a separate context, take the pinned rulespec-nz PR 104 checkout, recompute the sha256 digests of its published earners_levy artifacts and check them against its corpus journal, and perform a semantic comparison of the two encodings of regulation 4, classifying the result as byte-identical, semantically equal with byte differences, or semantically different.
output:
Fetched rulespec-nz (TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-nz, PR 104) at commit 7dd2b1ad8f13ff934aa53af562a34ea7451502f6. Computed sha256 of nz/regulations/acc/earners_levy.yaml and observed 5fe16742f55876ab33a6560793295346f3bad34912f09b7b84311436be2effed, matching corpus-journal entryIndex 3; computed sha256 of nz/regulations/acc/earners_levy.test.yaml and observed 43308ecb29fc26e30819d3657f89eb531d878f7e6ffa78e3712f709acf5906a4, matching corpus-journal entryIndex 2. Independently re-encoded reg 4 from corpus release nz-rulespec-2026-07-20 (content sha256 58089115f520cb99a3b90e3be503be63041ebe4a72bec69f24a2f115ed1ba196, cut from axiom-corpus commit 92ac9c1bedf62968eeea9a873361f49075364157; statute source data/corpus/sources/nz/regulation/2026-06-16-rulespec-nz-pco/regulation/public/2025/0018/wholeof.xml, sha256 f675c8ac89dab2ed08c6e228b93c90c65f0d9aa29425a783790f08599ef0f574, provision id LMS1019194), producing eeb3771924255c2f0c8b9cd393b22b8dc19667651b62322f42017e16e504e88b (scripts/fixtures/earners_levy.reencoded.yaml). The two digests differ, so the artifacts are not byte-identical, as expected for independent encodings.

Semantic comparison classification: (c) semantically different as whole modules, with substantive agreement on the shared regulation-4 rate core. Agreement: both encodings carry the same three standard levy rates with the same effective dates (2025-04-01, 2026-04-01, 2027-04-01, third band open-ended), numerically equivalent under unit conversion — our per-$100 statement values 1.45/1.52/1.59 (dtype Money, NZD) equal their fractional values 0.0145/0.0152/0.0159 (dtype Rate) exactly; both cite the same corpus citation path nz/regulation/regulation/public/2025/0018/regulation/4. Meaning-bearing differences: (1) Routing — our module encodes reg 4's exclusive three-way routing (paragraphs (a)/(b)/(c) of each subclause) as a derived selector with regulation-7 priority, reflecting reg 4's paragraph (b) limb 'regulation 6 applies (but regulation 7 does not apply)'; their module contains no routing or selector rule, its regulation-6 derived amount (acc_low_self_employed_minimum_levy_excluding_gst) is gated only on regulation 6's own hours/earnings conditions with no regulation-7 exclusion, and no rule in their module selects which amount is the levy payable for a person to whom multiple pathways apply. (2) Scope — their module spans regulations 4 through 9 plus extra-statutory Inland Revenue administration values (GST-inclusive rates 0.0167/0.0175/0.0183, maximum-earnings caps 152790/156641/160244, cents-rounding scale) across 12 rules (7 parameters, 5 derived), and applies the regulation-5 earnings cap inline in its standard-levy formulas; our module encodes regulation 4 only, across 2 rules (1 parameter, 1 derived), deferring the regulation-5 cap (noted via reg 4(4) 'subject to regulation 5') and the regulation-6/regulation-7 amount formulas as out of scope. (3) Proof-atom style — ours carries verbatim statute excerpts on all 8 proof atoms and cites regulation 2 for the commencement date; theirs uses citation-path-only atoms without excerpts, covering regulations 4-9. Honest counterpoint recorded: restricted to the regulation-4 rate schedule alone, the two encodings would classify as semantically equal with byte differences; the module-level classification is (c) because the regulation-6 pathway's applicability condition and the routing structure differ in meaning, not merely in representation, and because the module scopes are substantively different. Which reading each reflects: ours reads reg 4 as a rate schedule plus an exclusive routing directive with the reg-6/reg-7 formulas external; theirs reads the regulations package as a library of parameters and standalone component amounts, leaving reg 4's (b)/(c) selection and the reg-7-priority limb unencoded for downstream composition.
title: Rulespec interop POC: independent re-encoding and comparison of NZ ACC Earners' Levy regulation 4
summary: Two independent efforts encoded the same New Zealand accident-compensation levy regulation as machine-readable rules, and this record documents a first-hand comparison of the results. Both encodings agree on the levy rates and the dates they take effect, with values equivalent under a unit conversion. They differ in scope and in how the regulation's routing for self-employed people is structured, so the comparison is classified as semantically different at module level. Every file fingerprint in this record was independently recomputed from pinned sources during the comparison session.

org.civicaitools.rulespec-interop.comparison_summary: Shared reg-4 rate core agrees (same rates under per-$100 vs fractional representation, same effective dates); modules differ in meaning: their encoding omits reg 4(b)'s regulation-7 exclusion on the regulation-6 pathway and has no levy-payable routing rule, and the module scopes differ (their regs 4-9 plus IRD administration values across 12 rules vs our reg-4-only module of 2 rules).
